confirmed.title: Co-op setup hint promises 'The winner screen will pay @handle' but the co-op win screen never uses the handle (no payee, no Venmo button, no QR)
repro: Open https://music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app/index.html in a 393x852 window (fresh localStorage), tap New game
Tap the Co-op mode row (Mistakes-allowed stepper appears), toggle Buy-in on, type @kris-k into the Venmo handle field
Read the hint under the field: 'The winner screen will pay @kris-k'; the switch hint still reads 'Winner takes the pot'
Reduce to 2 players, set target to 5, Skip photo on both rows, Shuffle & start, play the co-op game to the win
Win screen shows 'THE POT $6 / Chipped in $3 each — settle it together.' with no payee line, no Open Venmo button, no QR
confirmed.expected: Either the setup copy reflects co-op (no single payee) or the co-op winner screen honours the promised handle with a payout link/QR.
confirmed.actual: Setup promises the handle will be paid; the co-op winner screen never uses it — no payee, no Venmo deeplink, no QR — and the 'Winner takes the pot' switch hint is also wrong for co-op, which has no individual winner.
sources: setup-options:Co-op setup promises "The winner screen will pay @handle" but the co-op winner screen never shows a payee, a Venmo button or a QR
confirmed.rationale: The pot math itself is correct ($6 pot, $3 each), so this is not S1 money-math. The co-op 'settle it together' end screen is plausibly the designed co-op behavior; the defect is setup copy actively promising a payout flow that never materialises — misleading copy with real money-coordination friction. That is the rubric's S3 (misleading copy), not S2 (no feature dead-ends; the game and the pot display survive). Single report, one cluster.

v1.reason: Reproduced end-to-end in a fresh Chrome session on the live site, UI-only. With Co-op selected, the buy-in hint reads verbatim "The winner screen will pay @kris-k" (verified visible and unoccluded; screenshot 04-hint-midview.png) and the switch hint reads "Winner takes the pot"; after playing a 2-player co-op game to the win at $3/head, the win screen shows "THE POT $6 / Chipped in $3 each — settle it together." with #win-pot-venmo hidden, #btn-venmo hidden, #win-qr empty, and "kris-k" nowhere in the block — 13/13 scripted checks passed, zero console errors (scratch/qa/round-7/verify-coop-venmo-promise-never-honored-1/). Source corroborates it is structural: ui.js paintBuyin() has no mode branch for the hint while the win renderer deliberately suppresses payee/button/QR in co-op ("Co-op has no one to pay"). Not BY_DESIGN: the deliberate part is the co-op win screen; the setup copy promising a payee in co-op is covered by neither the brief's by-design list nor the game rules. Severity holds at S3 (rubric: misleading copy): nothing dead-ends — pot math is right and the settle-together outcome works — so not S2; but it is a false promise about a real-money coordination flow plus a wrong "Winner takes the pot" line in a mode with no individual winner, so more than an S4 nit. One immaterial repro omission: the reported steps skip the single buyin-inc tap needed for $6/$3-each (as literally written the pot is $4/$2-each); the defect reproduces identically at any amount.

confirmed.title: Status line says 'Playing the preview.' over a paused, silent player when the vinyl is tapped while fast-flow autoplay is still buffering
repro: Open https://music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app/index.html?debug=1&seed=707 with network throttled (~400kbps / 400ms RTT; also seen organically at full speed)
New game, Skip photo on every row, Shuffle & start (defaults: classic mode, fast flow on)
On the pass screen tap #btn-pass-continue — fast flow starts loading/playing the song from this tap
Within ~1s, before any audio is audible, tap the big vinyl (#btn-play-song)
Watch the status line: audio stays paused at 0:00 with the play triangle and frozen countdown ring while the status reads 'Playing the preview.' for 6+ seconds; one more tap recovers
confirmed.expected: The tap is a pause toggle, so the status should read 'Paused — tap play to continue.' (the copy the app itself writes for a deliberate pause), or playback should continue — either way the UI matches the audio.
confirmed.actual: The pending play() promise from the autostart is rejected by the user's own pause (AbortError), wasInterrupted() maps that to success, and toggleAudio's success branch stamps 'Playing the preview.' after the pause branch already wrote the honest copy — leaving a paused, silent player captioned as playing until the next tap.
sources: adv-expert:Audio status line says "Playing the preview." over a paused, silent player when the vinyl is tapped during the preview's load window
perf-network:Status line says "Playing the preview." over a paused, silent player when the vinyl is tapped while fast-flow autoplay is still buffering
confirmed.rationale: Both reports name the same trigger (vinyl tap during the fast-flow autostart's play() settlement window), the same observable (paused at t=0, play triangle, 'Playing the preview.'), and the same mechanism in audio.js/ui.js — one root defect seen by two testers. Audio itself is not broken and one tap recovers, so this is not S2 feature-broken; it is a UI stating a falsehood during a recoverable race — the rubric's misleading copy / janky-but-recoverable S3. Both reporters independently landed on S3. The perf-network repro is chosen as best: deterministic script, seed, throttle numbers, and the recovery step.

v1.reason: Reproduced first attempt in my own fresh real-Chrome session (canPlayType AAC = "probably") with the exact reported steps: seed 707, fast-flow defaults, ~400kbps/400ms CDP throttle applied after setup, tap #btn-pass-continue, tap #btn-play-song 1s later. For 8 consecutive sampled seconds the audio element sat paused at currentTime=0 with the button labelled "Play song 31s" (play triangle, frozen ring — screenshot mid-lie.png) while #audio-status read "Playing the preview." — the finding's "6+ seconds" is if anything understated, since the lie persisted until the next tap. One recovery tap resumed playback (t=3.95s, paused=false, button "Pause"). Mechanism verified in source: fast-flow pass-continue calls toggleAudio (ui.js:4416-4420); the vinyl tap's pause branch writes the honest "Paused — tap play to continue." (ui.js:2359-2367); the pause rejects the autostart's awaited play() with AbortError, wasInterrupted maps it to started=true (audio.js:974-1016, 1012), and the autostart's success branch overwrites the status with "Playing the preview." (ui.js:2391-2403). Not BY_DESIGN — the comment at ui.js:2361 shows the app deliberately fixed this exact falsehood on the direct-pause path; this race is a surviving hole. Not S2 — audio works and one tap recovers; rubric's "misleading copy / janky-but-recoverable flow" = S3. Evidence: scratch/qa/round-7/verify-audio-status-lies-playing-over-paused-1/{verify.mjs,mid-lie.png,final-state.png,after-recovery.png}.

confirmed.title: listen.html footnote and wordmark render at 3.77:1 contrast, below the WCAG AA 4.5:1 minimum for normal-size text
repro: Open https://music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app/listen.html on a 393x852 viewport (no game payload needed)
In devtools read getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.footnote')).color and getComputedStyle(document.body).backgroundColor
Compute the WCAG contrast of rgb(109,103,136) text on the rgb(8,7,12) background: 3.77:1, below the 4.5:1 AA minimum; the .wordmark eyebrow (11.52px) uses the same token
confirmed.expected: The informational footnote 'Only the host's screen knows the year.' (12.48px normal weight) meets the 4.5:1 AA minimum, like every other measured text on the site (the scan hint measures 8.22:1; all main-app text passes).
confirmed.actual: Both .footnote and .wordmark use rgb(109,103,136) on rgb(8,7,12), measuring 3.77:1 — below AA for normal-size text.
sources: a11y:listen.html footnote and wordmark text render at 3.77:1 contrast where WCAG AA requires 4.5:1
confirmed.rationale: The rubric names 'minor a11y (missing label, weak contrast)' explicitly under S3 — this is exactly that. Not S2: no trap, no unreachable control, and only one informational line plus a logotype-arguable wordmark are affected. Hand-verified luminance math and distinct from the prior round's wording finding on the same footnote, so not a duplicate of anything.

v1.reason: Reproduced live in a fresh real-Chrome session at 393x852 (script: scratch/qa/round-7/verify-listen-page-footnote-contrast-below-aa-1/verify.mjs): .footnote computes rgb(109,103,136) at 12.48px/400 and .wordmark rgb(109,103,136) at 11.52px/700 on body rgb(8,7,12); WCAG contrast is 3.77:1 both by in-page computation and my independent hand math, below the 4.5:1 AA minimum for normal-size text (neither element is WCAG-large; the bold wordmark is only 11.52px vs the 18.66px bold threshold). Source confirms the tokens (--ink-faint: #6d6788 on --bg: #08070c in public/music/listen.css) and no lighter ancestor backdrop rescues the ratio. The wordmark alone would be logotype-arguable under WCAG 1.4.3, but the footnote is plain informational copy with no exemption, so the finding stands on it regardless. Not in the brief's by-design list, and no duplicate in rounds 1-6 (only vendored jsQR hex coincidences). Rubric names "weak contrast" explicitly under S3; proposed severity is exactly right — no trap or hidden control to justify S2, no basis to shave to S4.

confirmed.title: Setup edits made in the last ~500ms before a reload are silently lost — draft save is debounced with no pagehide/visibilitychange flush
repro: Open https://music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app/index.html fresh (clear site data), tap New game
Type a player name, set 'First to' down to 5, toggle the $2 buy-in on, type a Venmo handle
Within half a second of the last edit, reload the page (pull-to-refresh, or an app-switch that discards the tab)
Tap New game again: names come back but target reverts 5→10, buy-in reverts to off, the handle is blank; identical edits followed by a 700ms wait before reload restore everything
confirmed.expected: The whole half-edited form comes back — the code's own comment says 'everything set on this screen persists'.
confirmed.actual: saveSetupDraft() fires only on a 500ms debounce timer and nothing flushes it on pagehide/beforeunload/visibilitychange (confirmed by grep of ui.js), so any edit inside the debounce window is lost on an immediate reload or tab eviction.
sources: persistence:Setup edits made in the last ~500ms before a reload are silently lost (draft save is debounced with no pagehide flush)
confirmed.rationale: Not S1 data loss: the rubric's data loss covers a saved game/roster/stake vanishing, and no game has started — this is a pre-game draft losing edits made inside a 500ms window, requiring an app-switch-plus-tab-eviction or instant pull-to-refresh to hit. Recoverable by re-entering, narrow trigger window, well-evidenced mechanism. Subtle inconsistency against the app's own persistence promise → S4, matching the reporter. The buy-in-toggle-silently-off wrinkle is the strongest argument for S3; verification can promote it if the realistic app-switch path reproduces easily.

v1.reason: Reproduced on the first attempt, exactly as written, against the live site in a fresh browser context (script + 4 screenshots in scratch/qa/round-7/verify-setup-draft-debounce-lost-on-reload-1/). Phase A: typed a name, waited 800ms (roster settles), then in one <500ms burst stepped First-to 10->5, toggled buy-in on via its label, typed '@fabian-pays', and reloaded immediately. Pre-reload UI showed target 5 / buy-in on / handle filled; localStorage 'music-timeline:v1:setup' was null at reload; after reload the name survived but target reverted to 10, buy-in was off, handle blank. Phase B control: identical edits plus a 700ms settle before reload restored everything (draft present with target 5, buyin.enabled true, handle intact) — matching the finding's claimed contrast precisely. Code corroborates the mechanism: queueSetupSave is a 500ms setTimeout debounce (public/music/ui.js:750-756), every setup control routes through it, grep finds no pagehide/beforeunload/visibilitychange flush anywhere in ui.js (only confetti.js listens to visibilitychange, for animation), and the comment at ui.js:724-726 explicitly promises 'everything set on this screen persists.' Not by-design (the brief's list doesn't cover it and the code's own comment contradicts it). Severity stays S4 per the rubric: no saved game/roster/stake vanishes (roster survived; only never-persisted edits inside a half-second window are lost, pre-game), recoverable by re-entering, and the reverted state is plainly visible on the setup screen the user returns to — a subtle inconsistency against the app's own persistence promise, not S3 jank; no hard evidence to upgrade since the silent-money angle requires the host to ignore the visible buy-in toggle on the screen they are actively configuring.

confirmed.title: Setup accepts two identical player names, so the pass screen and standings show indistinguishable duplicate players
repro: Fresh page, clear localStorage, load /index.html, tap New game (4 rows pre-filled 'Player 1'..'Player 4')
Overwrite row 2's value with 'Player 1' (or name two rows 'Alex')
Tap Skip photo on every row, then Shuffle & start
Pass screen reads 'PASS THE PHONE TO Player 1, then Player 1'; standings list two 'Player 1' rows, disambiguated only by avatar color and PLAYING NOW / UP NEXT badges
confirmed.expected: A guard or nudge against two identical names, or a visible differentiator beyond avatar color.
confirmed.actual: Duplicate names are accepted silently; internal game state stays correct (players are separate), but both pass-screen hero and standings display identical names.
sources: first-run:Pass screen can still show two players with the same name when the user manually types a name that duplicates a pre-filled row (e.g. overwrites row 2 with 'Player 1')
confirmed.rationale: Borderline by-design — the duplicate is user-typed into pre-filled real values, the round-6 auto-name fix itself is confirmed working, and game state is internally correct. But two family members genuinely sharing a name (two Alexes) is a realistic party scenario, so it is a plausible polish defect rather than pure user error; per instructions it passes to verification rather than being dropped here. No wrong outcome, nothing broken, avatar color and turn badges partially disambiguate → S4 nit, as the reporter proposed.

v1.reason: Reproduced first try in a fresh Chrome session on the live site, exactly per the filed steps, plus the two-Alexes variant. Overwriting row 2 with 'Player 1' produced no warning or nudge (screenshot of setup screen confirms; start button never disabled), and after Shuffle & start the pass hero read 'PASS THE PHONE TO Player 1 / then Player 1' while standings listed two 'Player 1' rows distinguished only by avatar color and PLAYING NOW/UP NEXT badges. __timeline.state confirms internal correctness (distinct ids p1/p2). Not BY_DESIGN: the brief's list doesn't cover it, and ui.js's own comments (line ~1803) describe this exact pass-screen rendering as a bug when the app self-minted it — the existing dedupe only guards auto-placeholders, not user-typed names. The title's 'indistinguishable' is slightly strong (badges/colors partially disambiguate) but the finding body concedes that, so no material exaggeration. Rubric: no wrong outcome, nothing broken, fully recoverable — polish-level inconsistency, S4 as proposed. Evidence: scratch/qa/round-7/verify-duplicate-player-names-accepted-silently-1/ (verify.mjs + 4 screenshots).

coverage.coverage: All mission areas tested against the live site with real Chrome, ~15 min, 7 scripted sessions under scratch/qa/round-7/first-run/, pageerror/console-error captured in every session — zero page errors, zero console errors across all runs. (1) Fresh visitor: localStorage cleared; home at 320/375/393/428/768/1450/852x393 landscape — no horizontal overflow at any size, no resume card for a new visitor, deck stat renders ('1185 songs · 1950–2025'). (2) How-to-play read end to end (full text saved to rules-text.txt): no typos found; every rule statement matches the brief (targets 5/10/15, token economy −1 challenge / +1 name-it / −3 buy, 4 modes incl. co-op shared pool of 6 and mistake limit 3, streak bonus, buy-in never charges); no overflow at 320. (3) manifest.json 200 with valid name/icons/start_url/display; icon.svg + apple-touch-icon.png both 200; service worker registers and activates; second visit loads clean with no phantom resume card. (4) Resume: 5-player game saved mid-turn (turn 2, gap selected after draw), reload, resume card shows correct roster; after resume turn/activeIndex/players (names+tokens+timelines)/deck length/mode/target/options all byte-identical; a second probe confirmed the exact in-flight drawn card (same song id), the selected gap, and the Place button all survive reload. (5) Menu sheet from pass, play, and reveal (home deliberately has no menu button): all rows present (Scoreboard, How to play, 4 toggles, Play-songs-with select, Home, End game, done); Scoreboard and Rules round-trip back to the originating screen; Home keeps the game saved and resume works; Esc closes; opening menu on reveal cancels armed auto-next; End game double-tap confirm works and lands on the win screen with correct 'ahead when it ended' standings. (6) Round-6 fix probes: blank/whitespace names after row add/remove churn in 5 orderings always take the lowest unused 'Player N' with zero duplicates (the fix holds); pass-hero name clamp verified at 320/375/393/428 with unbroken 16 W's, a two-word 16-char name, a long unbroken realistic name, and a short control — no document overflow, hero and hint never clipped, short names keep full 40px size, screenshots visually confirmed. Not covered (other missions own it): audio playback depth, QR/listen page, offline mode, full game-rule outcomes. The one reported finding is a boundary case of the round-6 name fix (manual duplicates still allowed) reported honestly as S4/medium — it may legitimately adjudicate as by-design.

Mission: Setup players & roster, on the live Vercel site, real Chrome, UI-only via Playwright (scripts + screenshots in scratch/qa/round-7/roster/). Tested: (1) bounds — default 4 rows, remove disabled at 2 with honest title "At least two players", add stops at 8, no duplicate placeholders at 8, added rows reuse the lowest unused "Player N"; (2) photo gate — Start honestly disabled with matching visible reason + button title at 4 outstanding and at 1 outstanding, Skip photo toggles cleanly both ways (aria-pressed, data-photo-state, "Using their initial"), photo upload via setInputFiles on the row's real file input registers (data:image src, state=photo), gate lifts and game starts; (3) round-6 blank-name fix — four removal/blank orderings (remove P2+blank P3; blank two rows; manual "Player 2" collision; remove first+last, add two, blank both) plus blank-name-WITH-photo: every start produced distinct names taking the lowest unused Player N; (4) round-6 pass-hero clamp — 2 players named 16 unbroken W's and two-word 16-char at 320/375/393/428: zero horizontal overflow, name contained, hint line fully visible (screenshots read); (5) tricky names — 40-char input clips at 16 with the countdown counter appearing, emoji name plays/renders on pass+scoreboard and round-trips its avatar library, whitespace-only becomes lowest unused Player N, three duplicate Sams (incl. case-folded "sam") all seated with distinct seat colors, 3 standings rows, independent card counts after a placement; (6) guest list — chips appear after a game with photos intact, previous line-up pre-seated with photo, chip disabled "already playing" when seated, enabled when unseated, re-seats with photo, true-full table (8 touched rows) disables free chip with visible "table is full" and re-enables when a seat frees, edit mode toggles (aria-pressed/data-editing), armed two-tap forget with "Tap again to forget Bob" label removes person AND their avatar library from localStorage, forget of a seated person keeps her row+photo, forget button not tappable outside edit mode, empty list hides the block, game 2 starts cleanly afterward; (7) roster carry-through — pass hero/standings, play roster seats, and scoreboard all matched the 4-player roster incl. emoji and placeholder names. Zero pageerrors/console errors across ~15 fresh sessions. Five candidate issues raised by my probes were each investigated and refuted as by-design or script artifacts (count-based gate copy, finished-game "See final result" card, placeholder-filling chip, nested token-dot li count, entrance-animation screenshot frame). Not covered for time: photo persistence across a full game to the win screen avatar, and in-game rename flows (none exist in the UI).

~17 min of live testing on https://music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app/index.html (real Google Chrome, 320/375/393/428 widths), 10 throwaway scripts + screenshots under /Users/kriskibak/Developer/Projects/fabians-red-card/scratch/qa/round-7/setup-options/. Zero pageerror and zero console-error output in every single session.

ROUND-6 FIX PROBES (both hold — 01-r6-probes.mjs): blank/whitespace names now take the lowest UNUSED 'Player N' in three orders — remove row 2 then blank row 1 (Player 1/3/4), remove-to-2-then-add-back with one whitespace-only and one empty row (1/2/3/4), and the adversarial case where a real row is typed 'Player 2' and another is blanked (blank became 'Player 1', no duplicate). Pass-screen hero: 16 W's unbroken and a 16-char two-word name at 320/375/393/428 — no horizontal overflow, name box inside the viewport at every width, hint line on screen (screenshots read).

MISSION AREA. Modes: all four rows select on a row tap; mistake stepper shows only in co-op and clamps 1..9 with both buttons pinned at the bounds; mode/target/streak/mistake-limit all verified reaching game state (mode=coop, targetCards=5, streakBonus=true, mistakeLimit=4). Session hint: 4p/5=20–25, 4p/10=35–50, 4p/15=55–75, scales with seats in classic, correctly seat-independent in co-op. Target stepper pins at 5 and 15. Streak toggle on/off via label. Buy-in: block hidden until enabled, $2 default, clamps at $0 (dec pinned) and $100 (inc pinned), pot line exact at $0/$3/$100; pot arithmetic verified live at 2,3,4,5,6,7,8 players (removing and adding rows while the buy-in is open — every step correct), add-player pinned at 8.
